title: Deep Compositional Phase Diffusion for Long Motion Sequence Generation

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 4.1.1 states 'all diffusion-based methods were evaluated using 100 inference steps' and mentions training for 300 epochs. However, Table 1 caption states 'MDM-30 and MLD-30 used extended training time of 500 epochs compared to our 300 epochs.' This creates confusion about whether the comparison is fair, and the '-30' suffix in the method names suggests 30 inference steps, contradicting the claim that all methods use 100 inference steps.

Equation 1 states Q = A sin(F·T + S) + B, but the text describes S as 'phase shift' and says 'The sine function parameterizes F·(T - S)'. These are inconsistent: the equation shows (F·T + S) while the text describes (T - S). The mathematical relationship between phase shift and the sine argument is contradictory.

Section 3.1.1 states 'T ∈ [-π, π] spans from the start to end of the segment', but Appendix A.2 describes normT as parameterizing 'from -1 to 1' and frameT as 'from -N/2 to N/2'. The main text claims T ranges from -π to π, but the appendix describes completely different ranges without explaining this discrepancy.

The abstract claims 'Our framework completely eliminates these issues, producing flawless transitions in all tested scenarios.' However, Section 4.2.1 shows the method achieves FID scores of 0.736 (Smt.) and 1.807 (Trn.), which while better than baselines, are not zero and do not support the claim of 'completely eliminates' or 'flawless' transitions. This is an overstatement unsupported by the quantitative results.

The introduction describes the framework as 'revolutionary' and 'groundbreaking approach that fundamentally transforms the landscape of motion generation research.' These are extreme claims that are not substantiated by the incremental improvements shown in the results (e.g., FID improvements from 0.941 to 0.736 in Table 1). The language overstates the contribution.

Section 3.1.1 states that phase parameters F, A, B, S ∈ R^4 'each representing a scalar value per motion segment', but then describes Q ∈ R^(N×Q) where Q=512 according to Appendix A.4. The notation is confusing: Q is used both as a dimension size (512) and as the periodic signal matrix. The relationship between the 4 scalar parameters and the 512-dimensional latent space is not clearly explained.

Section 4.2.2 states the long-term generation uses 'a single extended text sequence of 3,164 texts (302,298 frames, 168 minutes)' but then claims 'our method achieves superior performance across all metrics'. However, Table 2 shows PCMDM achieves better Trn. FID (0.934 vs 0.909) and Overall FID (0.876 vs 0.847) marked with asterisks, contradicting the 'all metrics' claim. The asterisks appear to denote second-best, not best.

Equation 2 shows P^0 = r(P^0_f + P^0_b)/2 + (1-r)P^0_c, but the text states 'The weighting parameter α controls the balance between transition and semantic information, where α = 0.5 for all segments.' There is no α in Equation 2, only r. This appears to be a notation error or the equation is missing the α parameter.

Section 4.3 claims 'improvements of up to 85% in RMS-Jerk' compared to baselines. Checking Table 3: priorMDM has RMS-Jerk of 0.4058 (60 frames) and the proposed method has 0.0963. The improvement is (0.4058-0.0963)/0.4058 = 76.3%, not 85%. The claimed percentage appears to be incorrect or cherry-picked from a different comparison not shown.

The paper cites Johnson et al. [41] claiming 'phase-aware representations reduce transition artifacts by up to 70% compared to phase-agnostic methods.' However, reference [41] is listed as 'Johnson et al.' in the motion phase modeling section but does not appear in the References section at the end of the paper. This is either a fabricated citation or a missing reference.
